title: Fund the Safety Net, Not ICE
author: Jordan Liz
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/06/IMG_0858-1-680x510.jpeg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/06/22/fund-
the-safety-net-not-ice/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/06/IMG_0858-1-680x510.jpeg)

Homeless camp under a bridge, Portland, Oregon. Photo: Jeffrey St. Clair.

President Trump has made historically steep cuts to
[SNAP](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/30/snap-food-stamps-big-beautiful-
bill.html), [Medicaid](https://www.urban.org/urban-wire/medicaid-cuts-one-big-
beautiful-bill-act-leave-3-10-young-adults-vulnerable-losing), and [other
programs](https://www.splcenter.org/resources/guides/federal-budget-social-
safety-net-faq/), claiming we can’t afford them. Yet at the same time he and
his Republican allies have plowed record sums into ICE, even as [popular
support](https://maristpoll.marist.edu/polls/the-actions-of-ice-
february-2026/) for the agency has plunged.

In June, [Trump](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/10/trump-ice-70-billion-
immigration-funding.html) signed a $70 billion bill to fund Immigration and
Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Border Patrol through the remainder of his term.
This is the second Republican-led, multi-billion-dollar infusion into these
agencies since Trump retook office.

Last year, the [One Big Beautiful Bill Act](https://www.cato.org/blog/heres-
how-administration-plans-spend-largest-immigration-enforcement-funding-surge-
history) (OBBA) granted $75 billion to ICE and $65 billion to Customs and
Border Protection (CBP). That alone was seven times more than ICE’s annual
budget and four times more than CBP’s.

This funding is being used to supercharge Trump’s mass deportation regime. It
has allowed [ICE ](https://www.dhs.gov/news/2026/01/03/ice-announces-
historic-120-manpower-increase-thanks-recruitment-campaign-brought)to hire
12,000 new, [poorly trained](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/whistleblower-
warns-ice-has-slashed-training-for-recruits) officers and agents, leading
directly to the horrific scenes we saw in Minnesota and elsewhere.

Where else is this money going? To massive prisons.

Since 2025, [ICE](https://www.americanimmigrationcouncil.org/blog/ice-buys-
warehouses-immigration-detention/) has spent over $700 million to purchase
nine warehouses they intend to refurbish into new mega-detention centers. This
includes three “large-scale” facilities with 7,500 to 10,000 planned beds in
Georgia, Texas, and Pennsylvania. Reportedly, their plan is to spend [$38.3
billion](https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/research-reports/how-ices-
budget-boom-changing-immigration-detention) to acquire and retrofit 24
warehouses across the country.

To this end, ICE is extending their partnership with private prison companies
like [The Geo Group](https://www.americanimmigrationcouncil.org/blog/ice-buys-
warehouses-immigration-detention/), which has been widely criticized for[
abusing detainees](https://www.cnn.com/us/george-zoley-geo-group-ice-
immigration). Hunger and labor strikes have broken out at several of their
facilities [protesting inhumane living
conditions](https://www.commondreams.org/opinion/abolish-immigration-
detention) this year, including[ Delaney
Hall](https://apnews.com/article/immigration-detention-geo-group-protests-
delaney-hall-56b7adb202aa59b1b0e0121fba2df755) in New Jersey. [Deaths in these
facilities](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/death-rate-ice-immigrant-
detention-centers-more-than-doubles-under-trump-reuters-2026-06-17/) have
risen to record levels.

ICE is also expanding its biometric surveillance capabilities. In May 2026,
the [Department of Homeland
Security](https://www.npr.org/2026/05/27/nx-s1-5822429/ice-buys-iris-scanners-
tech-tools) (DHS) awarded a $25 million contract to the biometric firm BI2
Technologies. That amount is more than five times larger than the company’s
most recent DHS contract.

In short, ICE is preparing itself for more large-scale [Minnesota-style
invasions](https://www.cato.org/blog/ice-versus-fourth-amendment) of American
cities. Border Czar [Tom Homan](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2025/jul/21/trump-sanctuary-cities-noem-homan) has repeatedly threatened
to “flood” U.S. cities with ICE agents. There will be “more agents in the
community and more agents in the worksite,” he vowed last year.

Many of these threats have targeted New York City — one of the host cities for
the [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2022/06/new-
york-new-jersey-selected-host-city-2026-fifa-world-cup). “You’re going to see
more ICE agents than you’ve ever seen in New York City, and it’s coming,”
[Homan](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/08/ice-agents-new-york-
city-tom-homan) remarked in early June. “I just reviewed an operational plan.”

Amid a growing [affordability crisis](https://www.urban.org/data-
tools/american-affordability-tracker) and [massive
inflation](https://www.npr.org/2026/06/10/nx-s1-5853077/inflation-over-4-cpi-
gasoline-prices), Republicans are prioritizing ICE violence over helping
struggling families.

Despite spending tens of billions now on ICE, Trump insists that there simply
isn’t enough money to fund social programs. At a press conference
[Trump](https://x.com/factpostnews/status/2039444784083771629) remarked, “It’s
not possible for us to take care of day care, Medicaid, Medicare, all these
individual things… We have to take care of one thing: military protection.”

For Trump, there is money for federal agents that [injure, maim, and
kill](https://prospect.org/2026/01/29/ice-trump-killed-injured-list-dhs-cbp-
border-patrol-renee-good-alex-pretti/) anyone who gets in their way, but no
money for Medicare. There is money for more [detention
centers](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-44518942) that put children
in cages, but no money for childcare.

The problem is not simply that Trump refuses to fund programs that would help
working people. It’s also that his administration’s reckless spending actively
_hurts_ us. According to a new report, the [Social Security trust
fund](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/06/09/social-securitys-
reserves-could-be-depleted-by-2032/) is expected to reach depletion by the end
of 2032 — a year earlier than previously expected. The Social Security
trustees cite three factors: lower birth rates, less immigration, and the “Big
Beautiful Bill.”

Despite [right-wing fearmongering](https://www.propublica.org/article/trump-
administration-immigration-invasion-rhetoric-courts),
[immigrants](https://www.fwd.us/news/americans-and-immigration/) — whether
documented or undocumented — pay taxes, drive innovation, and contribute to
[economic growth](https://www.americanimmigrationcouncil.org/press-
release/immigrants-keep-economy-strong-as-congress-debates-mass-deportation/).
Funding an agency that makes life intentionally harder for immigrants drives
away the very people who have made — and continue to make — this nation great.

Now more than ever, we need
[politicians](https://www.newarab.com/news/progressives-are-sweeping-2026-us-
midterm-primaries) in Congress who will rein in Trump’s senseless spending,
work to [abolish ICE](https://www.kuow.org/stories/will-calls-to-abolish-ice-
sway-voters-in-2026-the-strategy-has-democrats-split), and put the people
first.

The post [Fund the Safety Net, Not
ICE](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/06/22/fund-the-safety-net-not-ice/)
appeared first on [CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
